title: Posterior tooth-pair laterality adds no demonstrated grip-strength prediction benefit across NHANES recruitment cohorts
abstract: Tooth counts discard the distribution of remaining teeth. We tested whether left-right imbalance of anatomically opposing natural posterior tooth pairs improves concurrent handgrip prediction beyond total teeth, total opposing posterior pairs and conventional predictors. A frozen sex-interacted spline ridge baseline trained in NHANES2011-2012 (n=2798) transferred to separately recruited2013-2014 (n=3218). Adding imbalance and its sex interaction changed examination-weighted MSE from 125.653 to 125.897 kg²; difference +0.244, joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-0.286,+2.053]. The registered improvement criterion failed; every sensitivity point comparison also worsened. This exploratory negative result tests a specific anatomical proxy, not measured bite contact, causal mastication mechanisms or equivalence. Validation is across recruitment cohorts within one survey program, not across independent programs.
